questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The blue is a beautiful colour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word 'The' before 'blue' is unnecessary in the context of the given sentence.
 
• In English, we generally do not use the definite article 'the' before colors unless we are referring to something specific that has already been mentioned or is known.
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence should be: ***Blue is a beautiful colour***.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Articles **(a, an, the)** are used before nouns to provide context. **'The'** is a definite article used to refer to something specific.
 
• When talking about colors in a general sense, we do not use the definite article **'the'**.
 
 
• **Example: *****Red** is a vibrant colour.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Nile is the ________ river of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, we are comparing** the Nile** river to all other rivers in the world.
 
• When making comparisons involving the highest degree, we use the** superlative** form of the** adjective**.
 
• The superlative form of the adjective** 'long**' is '**longest**'.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **'longest' **to indicate that the Nile is the river with the greatest length in the world.

Hence the correct sentence is ***The Nile is the longest river of the world*****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• While comparing two things, we use the comparative form of the adjective, such as 'longer'.
 
 
• **Example:** *The Nile is** longer **than the Amazon.*
 
 
 
• While comparing more than two objects or while indicating the highest degree, we use the **superlativ**e form of the adjective, such as '**longest**'.
 
 
• Example: *The Nile is the **longest** river in the world.*

__
 
• In the given sentence, the present perfect tense is required to indicate an action that started in the past and continues into the present.
 
• The correct form of the verb for the subject '**I**' in the present perfect tense is 'have been'.
 
• The present perfect tense is used to describe:
 
 
• An action or situation that started in the past and continues in the present.
 
• An action performed during a period that has not yet finished.
 
• A repeated action in an unspecified period between the past and now.
 
• An action that was completed in the very recent past, expressed by 'just'.
 
• An action when the time is not important or not specified.

• Option 2) is incorrect because '**had been ** is past perfect tense here, which indicates an action completed before another past action.
 
• Option 3)** ** is incorrect because** 'was here**' is simple past tense here , which indicates an action completed in the past.
 
• Option 4) is incorrect because **'has been** here 'has' is used with third person singular subjects (he, she, it).
